title: A map from a reduced scheme factors through a closed subscheme exactly set-theoretically
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let i:Z\to X be a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], and let Y be a reduced scheme [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. For a morphism f:Y\to X, f factors through i if and only if the set-theoretic image f(Y) is contained in i(Z). In particular, every morphism Y\to X factors through the reduction X_{\mathrm{red}}\to X [def-weil-pbc-scheme-reduction].

proof.text: If f = g ≫ i, every point f(y) is i(g(y)), so the range of f is contained in the range of i. The Lean proof supplies g.base y as the preimage.

Conversely apply the already proved source-library theorem AlgebraicGeometry.IsClosedImmersion.existsUnique_fac_of_range_subset_range (lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Morphisms/ClosedImmersion.lean, lines 181-191) to i, f and the range inclusion. Its hypotheses are exactly reducedness of Y and that i is a closed immersion. Forget uniqueness to obtain the required existential factorization. This source theorem is closed and uses the reduced-source ideal-kernel criterion, so no separate affine-section proof dependencies are needed here.

For the final clause take the source-library canonical morphism f.liftNilradical. Its equation f.liftNilradical_subschemeι is exactly the required composite equation (lean/WeilConjectures/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/IdealSheaf/Subscheme.lean, lines 405-425). The source construction is explicit from the scheme-theoretic image and the nilradical-kernel inclusion, with no arbitrary existence witness.
